bullets.title: Roku ($ROKU) flagged as M&A target; analyst maps 7 potential acquirers
bullets.body: Analyst frames Roku as 'the most eligible bachelor in streaming,' gaming out 7 potential suitors including Fox, Netflix, and Comcast, assessing balance sheet strength and strategic fit. Reuters separately reported Roku is exploring strategic options including an outright sale. One logical acquirer has reportedly already passed on the opportunity.

bullets.title: Amazon CEO Jassy reportedly triggered U.S. crackdown on Anthropic models via government discussions
bullets.body: WSJ reports Amazon CEO Andy Jassy's conversations with Trump administration officials prompted a sweeping government order blocking foreign access to Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models. AWS hosting of the Ant Group deployment is cited as a potential liability exposure for Amazon if a major cybersecurity incident follows.

bullets.title: NVDA flat ~10 months despite historic AI/tech run; AMD launches $3,999 Ryzen AI Halo to undercut NVDA's $4,679 DGX Spark
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts note NVDA has been essentially unchanged for close to 10 months during what one called 'the biggest technology run since the 1990s.' Separately, AMD announced its Ryzen AI Halo AI PC at $3,999 with 128GB memory, directly undercutting NVIDIA's DGX Spark at $4,679. AMD also claims Ryzen laptops outperform MacBook Neo for gaming and cut load times 95% with new shader delivery across all RDNA GPUs.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler leverage doubled to 1.8x in 6 months; $570B+ issuance in 2026 pushes spreads from AA to A
bullets.body: Fintwit credit analysis notes hyperscaler IG leverage rose from 0.9x in Q3 2025 to 1.8x now, rising >0.3x turns per quarter. $570B+ in total 2026 issuance includes AMZN's largest-ever Canadian bond and GOOGL's record JPY deal, as domestic demand saturates. Credit deterioration trajectory points toward BBB, with hyperscaler debt now larger than the entire energy sector. A separate ZeroHedge-cited analysis flags $1.8T in off-balance-sheet liabilities ($1T purchase commitments, $0.8T leases) and $520B in deferred earnings obscuring the true financial picture.

bullets.title: AI sovereignty/export control debate: model layer regulation seen as emerging framework; value accruing to app layer
bullets.body: Multiple accounts debate the Anthropic Fable/Mythos restriction as a preview of AI regulation at the model layer. One account argues value will accrue to model-agnostic application layers that implement routing between frontier and cheaper models. Another notes AI moats are now time-bound to under 90 days. A separate take: the restriction is bullish for sovereign AI buildouts and European capex acceleration; European semiconductor capex from a small base has outsized effect on scarcity trade.

bullets.title: Burry double-downs on ADBE at ~11x P/E near historical lows; also buying PYPL
bullets.body: Fintwit surfaces Burry's Substack thesis: market is punishing established, capital-efficient companies with real owner earnings while rewarding AI-narrative names. ADBE is highlighted trading at P/E ~11 near multi-year lows; Burry initiated PYPL at $49 in April and has been adding.

bullets.title: MSFT hasn't ruled out Xbox spinoff; CEO Nadella signals focus shift to monetization after 25-year investment
bullets.body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella acknowledged the company has struggled to monetize Xbox historically and is now focused on making the business sustainable. Separately, reporting confirms Microsoft hasn't ruled out spinning off Xbox as a strategic option.

bullets.title: DRAM prices surge up to 300% amid AI boom; WF₆ supply chain disruption affecting TSM, SK Hynix, Samsung
bullets.body: Headlines cite a global memory crunch with DRAM prices skyrocketing up to 300% amid AI demand. Separately, a detailed supply chain thread notes China's export controls on Japan disrupted ~25% of global WF₆ supply—a critical semiconductor manufacturing input for SK Hynix, Samsung, and TSM—flagging Foosung as a potential beneficiary play.

bullets.title: Sovereign AI thesis: nation states will train models on NVDA/AMD GPUs regardless of export controls
bullets.body: Fintwit analyst argues that sovereign AI model training will drive sustained GPU demand from nation states, with Nvidia and AMD chips as the only viable options for training at scale. Export controls will apply after capability thresholds, but GPU demand from state actors expected to persist.

bullets.title: Iran-US deal set for Sunday signing; Strait of Hormuz to open immediately
bullets.body: Trump confirmed Sunday signing of Iran deal with no monetary exchange, with the Strait of Hormuz opening to all traffic upon signing. Pakistan PM confirmed the US and Iran reached final text. Iran's Foreign Ministry later urged caution on exact timing. Separately, Iran launched drone attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait this weekend. Polymarket previously showed 83% probability of a permanent Iran-US ceasefire.

bullets.title: Tom Lee flags new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh as a drawdown risk factor
bullets.body: Fundstrat's Tom Lee cited testing of new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh as one of three drawdown risks building into markets. First FOMC meeting under Warsh is also described as unusual given the prior Chair will be present at the table amid a divided committee.

bullets.title: Goldman Sachs flags retail leverage amplifying market volatility; recommends owning vol
bullets.body: Goldman's Pasquariello notes retail investor leverage is adding fuel to market moves and recommends 'owning some vol' to simplify risk management in current environment. Separately, a record $90B flowed through leveraged ETFs in a single day during the digest window.

bullets.title: U.S. May budget deficit hits $293B, up from $42B in 2006 and $52B in 2016
bullets.body: Official US Treasury/FRED data shows May 2026 budget deficit at $293B, compared to $42B in May 2006 and $52B in May 2016. Separately, US debt interest costs now exceed both defense and Medicare spending at $3.6B/day.

bullets.title: India's IT consulting sector down ~50% on AI obsolescence fears; sector weight in Sensex shrinks from 25% to 14%
bullets.body: Fintwit notes India's stock market in a yearlong downtrend driven by IT consulting/outsourcing stocks falling ~50% on AI displacement concerns. The sector's weight in the Sensex has fallen from 25% at peak to 14%.

bullets.title: Cybersecurity stocks up 29.5% YTD vs. software barely breakeven
bullets.body: Fintwit analyst flags cybersecurity sector as the clear YTD outperformer at +29.5%, versus software which has barely broken even. Author maintains long exposure to cybersecurity names.

bullets.title: WBD faces California regulatory headwind after DOJ approved PSKY deal
bullets.body: California may block the DOJ-approved deal involving WBD and PSKY, with a state official signaling potential opposition to the federal approval.

bullets.title: COHR, LITE, NOK, CIEN grouped as photonics/optical favorites; photonics flagged as 'next' major theme
bullets.body: Fintwit account lists COHR, CIEN, NOK, and LITE among favorite companies in an optical/networking article. Separately, another account declares 'Photonics is next' as an investment theme, calling domestic laser makers 'national treasures.'

bullets.title: Tech sector P/E at 22.9x, in line with 10-year average; AI bubble 'not imminent' per one analyst
bullets.body: Bespoke data shows tech sector P/E at 22.9x, consistent with its 10-year average—valuations not stretched by historical standards. Separately, one analyst argues agentic AI is at Gartner's 'peak of inflated expectations' but there is more upside before the bubble peaks, while acknowledging AI investments will eventually end in a bubble.

bullets.title: TSLA: SpaceX/Tesla merger seen as 80% probable by 2027; SpaceX market cap now exceeds Tesla
bullets.body: CNBC Fast Money segment assigns 80% probability to a SpaceX/Tesla merger by 2027. SpaceX's market cap (at $165/share, ~$2.2T) has now exceeded Tesla's. One former TSLA bull has turned bearish, noting TSLA significantly underperformed NDX over 5 years.

bullets.title: AAPL in solid uptrend above 50-DMA; EU official meets Cook on child safety and AI
bullets.body: Technical analysis shows AAPL sitting just above its 50-day moving average in what appears to be a solid uptrend. Separately, EU's Costa had a 'productive discussion' with Apple CEO Tim Cook covering child safety, AI, and innovation.
